_comment: Machine-readable capability matrix for every agent-CLI adapter.
IMPORTANT: this file is VERIFIED, not merely maintained. tests/verify_capabilities.sh
exercises each adapter against mock CLI output and asserts that what actually happens
matches what is declared here. A hand-written matrix describing code inevitably drifts
into confident lies; the harness is what keeps this honest. If you change an adapter,
the verification test fails until this file agrees with reality.
Behavioral fields (verified by the harness): session_continuity, cost_reporting,
failure_detection, requires_jq. Descriptive fields (documentation only, not verifiable

opencode.notes: No confirmed skill-directory convention; SKILL.md is attached per invocation with -f/--file. Documented false-success quirk: exit 0 with non-empty stderr is treated as failure, which is why --print-logs must NOT be passed.

claude-code.notes: Only adapter implementing extract_cost_usd (total_cost_usd in the JSON envelope), so CUMULATIVE_BUDGET_USD is meaningful here and inert elsewhere. Headless mode requires an explicit tool/permission scope.

gemini-cli.notes: Uses its own --resume latest selector rather than an explicit captured id, so extract_session_id is a deliberate no-op. Project-scoped skills require a trusted workspace (/trust).

codex-cli.notes: Best-documented adapter: session id comes from a documented thread.started event, and failure from a documented turn.failed event. Non-empty stderr is NORMAL here (progress streams to stderr), so the opencode heuristic must not be reused.

hermes.notes: Session continuity is functionally ABSENT despite invoke_agent having a --resume code path: extract_session_id is a deliberate no-op (no confirmed structured-output flag), so the id file is never written and --resume is never passed. Declared 'explicit_id' until the verification harness caught it. Confirm a structured-output flag on your installed version, implement extract_session_id, then update this to 'explicit_id' — the harness will hold you to it. Supports explicit skill preloading with -s, which is more deterministic than description-matching.
